security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code examples, Mermaid syntax, and one preview link. No prompt injection, command execution intent, data exfiltration, or malicious behavior was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: 2. **Set subgraph fills to `none`** — Allows subgraphs to adapt to any background
3. **Use rounded shapes** — `([text])` for stadium shapes, `((text))` for circles
4. **No Font Awesome icons** — GitHub doesn't support `fa:fa-*` icons, they render as text
5. **Quote subgraph labels** — Use `subgraph Name["Label Text"]` syntax
- `stroke-dasharray:5 5` creates a dashed border (optional, looks clean)
- `color:#...` sets the subgraph label colour to match the border

2. **No HTML** — Can't use `
` or other HTML in node labels
3. **Quote labels with spaces** — `subgraph X["Label"]` not `subgraph X [Label]`
4. **Test locally** — Use [mermaid.live](https://mermaid.live) to preview before committing

content.value_statement: Mermaid diagrams often lose readability across GitHub light and dark themes. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical styling rules for clear Markdown diagrams.
actual_capabilities: Provides a GitHub-compatible Mermaid flowchart template with reusable class definitions.
Recommends dark fills, light strokes, and white text for theme-safe node styling.
Shows how to style subgraphs with transparent fills and readable borders.
Lists Mermaid node shapes suited for users, actions, decisions, and storage.
Documents common GitHub Mermaid mistakes, including unsupported Font Awesome icons and HTML labels.
Gives color pairing examples for gray, purple, blue, orange, green, red, and teal nodes.
limitations: It is a guidance-only skill and does not render or validate diagrams automatically.
It focuses on GitHub Markdown, not every Mermaid renderer or extension.
It covers flowchart styling more deeply than sequence, class, or state diagrams.
It recommends visual conventions but cannot guarantee accessibility for every color choice.

use_cases.title: Architecture Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Create readable system flow diagrams that reviewers can view directly in GitHub pull requests.

use_cases.title: Process Documentation
use_cases.description: Convert process steps into clean Mermaid flowcharts with consistent colors and node shapes.

use_cases.title: Data Pipeline Mapping
use_cases.description: Document pipeline stages, decisions, and outputs with styling that works in light and dark themes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Flowchart
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple diagram
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub-compatible Mermaid flowchart for this process: [describe steps]. Use dark fills, light strokes, rounded nodes, and quoted subgraph labels.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup of Mermaid syntax and styling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Mermaid diagram for GitHub rendering issues. Fix subgraph labels, node shapes, color contrast, and unsupported icons while preserving the structure.

prompt_templates.title: Document a System Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mermaid architecture diagram for [system]. Group related services into transparent subgraphs and apply clear class styles for users, services, storage, and outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize Diagram Guidelines
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a reusable Mermaid style guide for our repository. Include color pairings, node shape rules, subgraph styling rules, and GitHub-specific limitations.

output_examples.input: A user submits a request, the service validates it, stores data, and returns a success result.
output_examples.output: A theme-safe flowchart plan with a user node, validation step, storage node, decision point, and success output.

output_examples.input: An existing diagram uses light node fills, unquoted subgraph labels, and Font Awesome icons.
output_examples.output: A corrected diagram approach using dark node fills, quoted labels, text-based labels, and transparent subgraphs.

output_examples.input: A team wants one diagram convention for pull requests and documentation.
output_examples.output: A concise style guide covering palette choices, rounded shapes, subgraph borders, and GitHub Markdown constraints.

best_practices: Use dark node fills with light strokes and white text for GitHub theme compatibility.
Quote subgraph labels that contain spaces to avoid Mermaid parse errors.
Keep class definitions near the top so diagram styling stays consistent and maintainable.
anti_patterns: Do not use Font Awesome icon syntax because GitHub renders it as plain text.
Do not use light fills with dark text when diagrams must work in dark mode.
Do not use colored subgraph fills when transparent fills can adapt to the page background.

faq.question: Does this skill generate diagrams automatically?
faq.answer: It provides instructions and templates that help an AI assistant create Mermaid diagrams. It does not include a renderer.

faq.question: Will the diagrams work in GitHub markdown?
faq.answer: The guidance is designed for GitHub Mermaid rendering and avoids unsupported icons and HTML labels.

faq.question: Why does it recommend dark fills?
faq.answer: Dark fills with light strokes keep nodes readable across light and dark GitHub themes.

faq.question: Can I use custom colors?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill recommends choosing a darker fill and a lighter stroke from the same color family.

faq.question: Does it support diagrams beyond flowcharts?
faq.answer: The examples focus on flowcharts. Some styling principles may still help with other Mermaid diagram types.

faq.question: Can it validate Mermaid syntax?
faq.answer: No. It suggests testing diagrams in a Mermaid preview tool before committing them.
